# `aitbc exchange order place`

Sign and place an AIT/ETH order. Under settlement the response carries the funding instruction — rendered as a hint above the JSON.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc exchange order place [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--side` | choice | — | yes | Order side |
| `--amount` | decimal | — | yes | AIT amount (8-decimal exact) |
| `--price` | decimal | — | yes | ETH price per AIT (within the oracle band) |
| `--expires-in` | integer | `1440` | no | Blocks until the order envelope expires |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet name or file path (this node's own wallet) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--chain-id` | text | — | no | Envelope chain_id (default: island credentials) |
| `--exchange-url` | text | — | no | Override exchange service base URL |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc exchange order place --side <side> --amount <amount> --price <price>
```
